Every topic has three pieces: the **theory** (this section), **practice** with solutions and a one-page **review sheet**. Study a module, do its practice without looking and mark the page as studied with the button under its title, so [My progress](progreso.en.qmd) knows where you are.

::: {.callout-tip title="Not sure where to start?"}
Follow the [study plan](guides/plan-de-estudio.en.qmd): it says what to do each week until December 18. The [home page](index.en.qmd) shows this week's tasks.
:::

## Part 1 · Abstract reasoning (30 minutes)

It is trained with **daily timed practice**, not by studying theory: 15–20 minutes a day beat one long session a week.

| Theory | Practice | Mock exam |
|---|---|---|
| [Abstract reasoning](01-razonamiento-abstracto/index.en.qmd): question types, the **FORMA-CPR** checklist, strategy for the 30 minutes | [50 exercises](01-razonamiento-abstracto/ejercicios.en.qmd) + unlimited figures in the [simulator](simulador/index.html) | [Reasoning #1](simulacros/simulacro-razonamiento-01.en.qmd) (30 questions, 30 min) |

## Part 2 · Technical test (90 minutes, in English)

Sorted by **priority** according to what candidates report ([research](guides/que-evalua-blend360.en.qmd)): SQL weighs the most and is asked against the clock. Hours are a guide.

| Priority | Topic | Hours | Theory | Practice | Review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | **SQL**: JOINs, aggregations, CTEs, window functions | 12 h | [SQL guide](02-sql/index.en.qmd) | [35 exercises](02-sql/ejercicios.en.qmd) · [SQL lab](simulador/index.html) | [Cheat sheet](cheatsheets/sql.en.qmd) |
| High | **Python** for data | 10 h | [Python guide](03-python/index.en.qmd) · [pandas](03-python/pandas.en.qmd) | [25 exercises in the lab](simulador/index.html) | [Cheat sheet](cheatsheets/python.en.qmd) |
| Medium | **Algorithms and data structures** | 8 h | [Guide](04-algoritmos-y-estructuras/index.en.qmd) | [20 problems in the lab](simulador/index.html) | [Cheat sheet](cheatsheets/algoritmos.en.qmd) |
| Medium | **AWS and data analytics on AWS** (Blend is an AWS Premier Partner) | 6 h | [Fundamentals](06-aws/index.en.qmd) · [data analytics](06-aws/analisis-de-datos.en.qmd) | [30 questions](06-aws/preguntas.en.qmd) | [Cheat sheet](cheatsheets/aws-y-bases-de-datos.en.qmd) |
| Medium | **Databases**: keys, normalisation, ACID, OLTP/OLAP | 4 h | [Guide](05-bases-de-datos/index.en.qmd) | Self-assessment at the end of the guide | [Cheat sheet](cheatsheets/aws-y-bases-de-datos.en.qmd) |
| Medium | **Problem solving**, logic and maths | 4 h | [Guide](07-resolucion-de-problemas/index.en.qmd) | Worked exercises in the guide | [Final review](cheatsheets/repaso-final-48h.en.qmd) |
| Medium (high for Data Science) | **Statistics and machine learning** | 6 h | [Guide](08-estadistica-y-ml/index.en.qmd) | [25 questions](08-estadistica-y-ml/preguntas.en.qmd) | [Cheat sheet](cheatsheets/estadistica-ml.en.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note title="What about the Python and algorithm exercises?"}
They live in `.py` files with an automatic grader. Do them in the **[simulator's code lab](simulador/index.html)** (in the browser, also on your phone) or on your computer with `python3 test_ejercicios.py` and `python3 test_problemas.py` (see the [Python](03-python/index.en.qmd) and [algorithms](04-algoritmos-y-estructuras/index.en.qmd) guides).
:::

## How to study a module

<ol class="b-steps">
<li class="b-step"><strong>Before: look at the self-assessment</strong><p>Read the questions at the end of the module first. You then read looking for answers instead of turning pages.</p></li>
<li class="b-step"><strong>During: write and run</strong><p>Copy the SQL and Python examples into the <a href="simulador/index.html">lab</a> and change them. What you write sticks; what you only read does not.</p></li>
<li class="b-step"><strong>After: practise without looking</strong><p>Do the exercises without opening the solution. When you miss one, write the mistake and the rule in the <a href="progreso.en.html#mistake-notebook">mistake notebook</a>.</p></li>
<li class="b-step"><strong>Two days later: redo the misses</strong><p>Redo only what you missed. If it works, mark it as mastered; if not, go back to that point of the theory.</p></li>
</ol>

## Techniques that pay off most

| Technique | How to apply it here |
|---|---|
| **Active recall** | Try to answer before looking. Solutions are hidden on purpose: open them only after trying. |
| **Spaced repetition** | 20 new [flashcards](flashcards/index.en.qmd) a day in Anki + the reviews. The mistake notebook schedules your reviews. |
| **Interleaved practice** | In the simulator, mix topics (technical mode) instead of 40 questions on one topic. |
| **Practise like the exam** | From week 3, everything is timed: 12 min per SQL problem, 1 min per multiple-choice question. |
| **Explain out loud (in English)** | Explain a query or an algorithm out loud in English: you train the topic and the interview at once. |
